facts: The respondent was enrolled as Sub-Inspector in the Delhi Police in the year 1967.
In 1984 the respondent was working as a Sub-Inspector in Special Security District, New Delhi and was posted at the residence of the then Prime Minister Mrs. Indira Gandhi for security purposes.
On 31st of October, 1984 the then Prime Minister was assassinated by two members of her security staff, namely, Sub-Inspector Beant Singh and Constable Satwant Singh of the Delhi Police.
In connection with the murder a criminal case was registered under Sections 307, 302 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 25, 27, 54, and 59 of the Arms Act.
The respondent was arrested in connection with the said criminal case.
In view of his arrest on 8th of December, 1984 the respondent was placed under suspension.
The order of suspension stated that a Departmental Enquiry will be conducted against the respondent.
The respondent filed an application before the Central Administrative Tribunal, Principal Bench, new Delhi, challenging his order of dismissal dated 16th of March, 1985.
He rayed for quashing the order and for a direction to the appellant herein to reinstate him in service with retrospective effect, with all consequential benefits.
issues: What is the scope of judicial review permissible in respect of an order of dismissal passed under second proviso Cl. (c) of Art. 311(2) of the Constitution?
Can the Court sit in appeal over the order or substitute its own satisfaction for the satisfaction of the President?
petitioner_arguments: The respondent should be dismissed from service under proviso (c) to Art. 311(2) in view of the material which was placed before it.
The order of dismissal dated 16th of March, 1985 is vitiated by mala fides or is based on wholly extraneous and/or irrelevant grounds.
respondent_arguments: There is no material before the President which is relevant for arriving at his satisfaction as to action being taken under Cl. (c) to the second proviso to Art. 311(2).
The Court should not sit in appeal over the order or substitute its own satisfaction for the satisfaction of the President.
court_reasoning: The satisfaction of the President can be examined within the limits laid down in S.R. Bommai and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors.
The order of the President can be examined to ascertain whether it is vitiated either by mala fides or is based on wholly extraneous and/or irrelevant grounds.

So long as there is material before the President which is relevant for arriving at his satisfaction as to action being taken under Cl. (c) to the second proviso to Art. 311(2), the Court would be bound by the order so passed.
holding: The respondent was dismissed from service under proviso (c) to Art. 311(2) in view of the material which was placed before it.
The order of dismissal dated 16th of March, 1985 is not vitiated by mala fides or is based on wholly extraneous and/or irrelevant grounds.
